assessments.title: Strategic AI Competency Survey
assessments.description: A short assessment on AI awareness, ethical use, and data privacy for city government employees. A Gmail address is required to register and ensure each employee only takes this assessment once.

questions.text: True or False: AI is capable of making final legal or budgetary decisions without human oversight.
options: True
False

questions.text: Under the Data Privacy Act of 2012 (RA 10173), is it acceptable to input citizen names or addresses into a public AI model without safeguards?
options: Yes, as long as the output looks accurate
No, this may violate data privacy requirements
Only if the citizen gave verbal consent
AI tools are exempt from the Data Privacy Act

questions.text: If an AI-generated public announcement contains an error, who is ultimately responsible?
options: The user who generated and published it
The IT Department
The AI software provider
No one — the AI is responsible

questions.text: Which best describes the difference between Generative AI (e.g. ChatGPT) and Automation (e.g. an Excel macro)?
options: Generative AI creates new content from learned patterns; automation follows fixed, pre-programmed rules
They are the same technology with different names
Automation is more advanced than Generative AI
Generative AI can only automate spreadsheets

questions.text: Which AI tool is most widely used by LGU Balanga employees today?
options: Claude (Anthropic)
Google Gemini
ChatGPT
Microsoft Copilot

questions.text: What is the most effective way to check if an AI-generated report is biased against a specific demographic or sector?
options: Re-read it once and assume it's fine
Ask a supervisor without further review
Cross-reference with official local data and test outputs across different demographic groups
Trust the AI's own confidence score
